purpose: Lidocaine cream is used to numb a small area of skin before a needle stick, minor procedure, or to relieve pain and itching from minor skin irritations, sunburn, insect bites, or hemorrhoids. It works right on the skin where you apply it, so you feel less pain or discomfort in that spot. Your doctor or pharmacist may also recommend it before certain cosmetic procedures like laser treatments.
how_it_works: Lidocaine works by temporarily blocking the nerve signals in the area where you put the cream. Think of it like putting your nerves on pause — they stop sending pain messages to your brain for a little while. Once the cream wears off, normal feeling comes back on its own.
common_side_effects: The most common side effects are mild and happen right where you apply the cream. You might notice some redness, mild swelling, a slight burning or stinging feeling at first, or temporary paleness of the skin. These usually go away quickly on their own.
warnings: Do not use this cream on broken skin, deep wounds, or in your eyes. Do not cover a large area of your body with it unless your doctor tells you to, because too much can be absorbed into your bloodstream and cause serious problems like dizziness, irregular heartbeat, or seizures. Keep it away from children and never use more than directed. Tell your doctor if you are pregnant, breastfeeding, or have any heart conditions before using this product.
typical_dosing: For most adults, a thin layer is applied to the affected area of skin and left on for the time recommended on the label or by your doctor — usually 20 to 60 minutes before a procedure. For skin irritation relief, it can be applied up to 3 to 4 times a day as needed. Always follow the directions on the package or as your doctor or pharmacist instructs you.
